title: Leray's theorem for quasi-coherent sheaves
statement:
Let $X$ be separated over an affine base $S=\Spec A$ and let
$\mathfrak U$ be an open affine covering. Then for every quasi-coherent
$\cO_X$-module $\cF$ and every $q\ge0$ there is an isomorphism of
$\Gamma(X,\cO_X)$-modules, hence of $A=\Gamma(S,\cO_S)$-modules (the edge
map of [det-thm-picard-cech] is one)

$$
\Cech^q(\mathfrak U,\cF)\overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow}H^q(X,\cF)
\qquad(q\ge0);
$$

in particular it is $k$-linear when $S=\Spec k$.

proof.text: Write the covering as $(U_i)_{i\in I}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection] to the given separated morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Thus two affine opens intersect in an affine open. Induct on the length of a nonempty tuple: length one is the covering hypothesis; intersect the affine intersection of the first $p+1$ opens with the last affine open for the induction step. Hence every $U_{i_0\dots i_p}$ is affine, including repeated indices and empty intersections. No affineness of the intersection of the empty family (which would be $X$) is asserted.

source.place: Tag 01KP, label lemma-characterize-separated (1)(a); blueprint proof Step 1

proof.text: Restrict $\mathcal F$ to each tuple intersection. It remains quasi-coherent by [pqf-def-coherent]: a point of the open has a standard open $D(f)$ inside it and inside an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $\mathcal F|_{\operatorname{Spec}B}=\widetilde M$, and $\mathcal F|_{D(f)}=\widetilde{M_f}$. By Step 1 and [det-lem-picard-affine], its cohomology there vanishes in every positive degree. Apply [det-thm-picard-cech] to the underlying abelian sheaf $\mathcal F_{ab}$ on the Zariski site (the opens form a set, finite fibre products are intersections, and the given family covers $X$). Its row terms $H^b(W,\mathcal F_{ab})$, cohomology over the object $W=U_{i_0\dots i_p}$, are the cohomology of $\mathcal F_{ab}|_W$ on the localized site, which is $W_{\rm Zar}$, by [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-over-object-localization]; by [lem-sc-zariski-module-abelian-cohomology-agree] for the scheme $W$ these are the module cohomology groups $H^b(W,\mathcal F|_W)$ to which the vanishing just proved applies, and by the same node for $X$ the abutment $H^n(X,\mathcal F_{ab})$ is $H^n(X,\mathcal F)$, the identifications being the identity in degree zero. All terms of the Cech complex of $\mathcal H^b(\mathcal F)$ are zero for $b>0$, so $E_2^{a,b}=0$ there. In row zero $\mathcal H^0(\mathcal F)(V)=\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)$, giving $E_2^{a,0}=\check H^a(\mathfrak U,\mathcal F)$. For $r\ge2$, differentials out of this row have negative second index and differentials into it start in a zero positive row. Thus $E_\infty^{q,0}=E_2^{q,0}$. In total degree $q$ the finite abutment filtration has only this one nonzero graded piece; its edge map is therefore bijective, also for $q=0$.

proof.text: Use the canonical comparison, rather than choosing an arbitrary bijection. By [lem-sc-cech-comparison-map-iso-affine] the affine-intersection cover of Step 1 makes the canonical comparison an isomorphism. Its precise normalization is [def-sc-module-cech-comparison]: for an injective resolution, let $T$ be the total Cech-resolution double complex, $\alpha:\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)\to T$ the restriction augmentation and $\beta:\check C^\bullet(\mathfrak U,\mathcal F)\to T$ the resolution augmentation; the map is $H^q(\alpha)^{-1}H^q(\beta)$. This is the edge map in Step 2, read as in the module form of the construction (Stacks 01ES, the source of this item), whose double complex is formed with an injective resolution in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ and whose $E_2$ terms and abutment are those of Step 2 through the identifications made there: the zero-resolution row enters the total complex by $\beta$, and the abutment is identified with sheaf cohomology by $\alpha$. If the two total-complex conventions order the indices oppositely, multiplication in bidegree $(a,b)$ by $(-1)^{ab}$ intertwines $d_C+(-1)^a d_I$ and $d_I+(-1)^b d_C$ and is the identity on both axes, so both augmentations, and hence the comparison, agree.

source.place: Tag 01EQ, label lemma-cech-cohomology, alpha and beta in the proof; Tag 01ET; blueprint proof Step 2 (specified edge map)

proof.text: Put $R=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. For $r\in R$, multiplication $m_r:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. The naturality equation of [lem-sc-cech-comparison-map-naturality], applied to $m_r$, says $c_{\mathcal F}\check H^q(m_r)=H^q(m_r)c_{\mathcal F}$. The first induced map is multiplication by $r$ on sections term by term and hence on Cech cohomology; the second is the induced $R$-action on sheaf cohomology. Thus $c_{\mathcal F}(rx)=r c_{\mathcal F}(x)$. Together with Step 3 this gives the claimed $R$-module isomorphism. For $a\in A$, its action is that of the image of $a$ under $A\to R$, so the same equation proves $A$-linearity; taking $A=k$ proves the field assertion.
